blocks.headline: Power out tonight? *5 rules* that keep your family safe.
blocks.narration: If the power goes out tonight, these five rules matter more than anything in your pantry.
blocks.scene: a dark farmhouse living room lit by one camping lantern on a wooden table, frost on the window, winter night, pine trees outside

blocks.headline: 1. Generator: *20 feet* from the house.
lines: o|Never in the garage, even with the door open
o|Exhaust away from windows and doors
blocks.narration: Run a generator at least twenty feet from the house. Never in the garage, even with the door open.
blocks.scene: a portable generator sitting on a gravel driveway far from a farmhouse, overcast winter afternoon, extension cord across the yard

blocks.headline: 2. Grills and camp stoves stay *outside*.
lines: o|Never heat the house with the oven
blocks.narration: Grills and camp stoves stay outside. And never use your oven or stovetop to heat the house.
blocks.scene: a charcoal grill on an open back porch with light snow on the railing, winter dusk

blocks.headline: 3. A *battery* CO alarm.
blocks.narration: Put a battery carbon monoxide alarm outside every sleeping area, and test it before the storm hits.
blocks.scene: a white carbon monoxide alarm mounted on a hallway wall outside a bedroom door, soft lamp light

blocks.headline: 4. Too cold inside? *Go somewhere warm.*
lines: b|A warming center or a warm friend's house
b|Older adults and babies chill fastest
blocks.narration: In the 2021 Texas freeze, the cold itself took the most lives. If your house gets dangerously cold, go somewhere warm.
blocks.scene: a pickup truck on an icy East Texas country road at dusk, headlights on, frozen pine trees

blocks.headline: 5. Keep the fridge *shut*.
blocks.narration: Keep the fridge closed. Food stays safe about four hours. A full freezer holds about two days, half full about one.
blocks.scene: a closed white refrigerator in a dim farmhouse kitchen during a power outage, candle on the counter

blocks.headline: Comment *READY*
blocks.narration: Comment ready, and we'll message you the ninety day kit. Thirteen printable pages, nine dollars.
blocks.scene: a printed home emergency checklist on a clipboard on a kitchen table beside a mug of coffee and a pencil, morning window light
